title: Geodesic stability for memoryless binary long-lived consensus
review_status: full-text audit complete; model assumptions, main conjecture, general zig-zag lower bounds, selected parameter cases and geodesic path restriction checked
venue_year_verified: arXiv first submitted 2011-02-20; Journal of Computer and System Sciences 81(7), 1210–1220 (2015), DOI 10.1016/j.jcss.2015.03.002; frame stratification uses arXiv first-submission year
evidence_note: The paper states inst(n,t)=2t+1 as a conjecture and gives constructions/lower bounds; Theorem 4.1 proves the conjecture for t=0 and t=1, while further theorems cover selected parameter cases. The general equality is not proved in this paper. Model is binary, memoryless, worst-case geodesic input paths.

title: Locally Repairable Codes
review_status: full-text audit complete; locality definition, distance/storage tradeoff, achievability conditions and distinction from bandwidth/disk I/O checked
venue_year_verified: arXiv first submitted 2012-06-17; v2 dated 2014-05-03; IEEE Transactions on Information Theory 60(10), 5843–5855 (2014), DOI 10.1109/TIT.2014.2325570
evidence_note: Locality counts other coded symbols accessed. The paper explicitly distinguishes this from repair bandwidth and bits read/disk I/O. Lower locality can cost distance or storage and does not establish lower end-to-end repair time or traffic.

title: XORing Elephants: Novel Erasure Codes for Big Data
review_status: full-text audit complete; code construction, HDFS-Xorbas implementation, EC2 and Facebook test-cluster setup, failure schedule, I/O/network/time metrics, storage overhead and saturation limits checked
sections_checked: HDFS bytes read, network traffic and repair duration results
evidence_note: In the reported EC2 prototype, HDFS-Xorbas reads 41–52% as much data and repairs 25–45% faster than HDFS-RS, with roughly 14% additional storage. The authors estimate 14.3% more blocks exposed to random failure; test network peaks were not saturated. Controlled prototype, not production randomized evidence.

title: Average Binary Long-Lived Consensus: Quantifying the Stabilizing Role Played by Memory
review_status: targeted counterevidence full text inspected; geodesic versus random-walk objectives, memoryless rule examples and one-bit memory construction checked
venue_year_verified: 2008 article; full primary-source PDF repository version
evidence_note: Worst-case geodesic and random-walk average objectives rank rules differently in the paper’s binary model. A one-bit-memory construction achieves its average optimum. No deployment traces were analyzed.

title: Practical Design Considerations for Wide Locally Recoverable Codes (LRCs)
review_status: targeted follow-up full text inspected; Google cluster stripe data, matched-width/overhead counterfactual replay, erasure-pattern sensitivity and operational tradeoffs checked
sections_checked: Uniform Cauchy LRC replay and recovery results
venue_year_verified: USENIX FAST 2023; Google Research primary landing page and full text
evidence_note: On 278 unavailable stripes, the deployed wide-code configuration recovered 0 before restoration and a same-width/overhead Uniform Cauchy LRC replay recovered 92 (33%). This is counterfactual trace replay, not a live randomized replacement; code layout and erasure patterns matter beyond width/overhead alone.
